thread:
jin: Quick share — ran a KV-cache paging + prefetcher sweep across GPU/region mix with a simulated seqlen distribution. wanted to flag some surprising p99 behavior in eu-west1.

maria: Nice, did you include both flash-attention and cuda-fmha kernel builds?

jin: Yep. Ran 3 kernel configs: `fmha-default`, `fmha-flash`, and `fmha-ptx-optim`. Also toggled prefetcher on/off and two eviction policies (LRU, TTL-based).

ethan: What's the seqlen mix you used? Real workloads skew short usually.

jin: Used a 3-bucket mix mimicking product traces: `short: 65%, medium: 25%, long: 10%` (short=8, med=64, long=1024). Also ran an extreme-long test (30% long) to stress paging.

perf-bot: benchmark run finished: id=kv-prefetch-1768342100
Results snapshot: us-west1(A100): hitrate=94.2%, p50=12ms, p95=28ms, p99=65ms; eu-west1(H100): hitrate=89.7%, p50=14ms, p95=34ms, p99=142ms; asia-east(T4): hitrate=82.1%, p50=20ms, p95=60ms, p99=210ms

olivia: That p99 jump in eu-west1 — did paging frequency correlate with host->device copy stalls? Any KV page-out rate logs?

jin: Yes. When long requests hit (~10% of traffic), page-outs spiked and prefetcher caught ~40% of upcoming blocks on A100 but only ~22% on H100 in eu-west1. Kernel dispatch on H100 queued longer due to smaller FIFO depth on that infra tier we use there.

maria: Can you paste the command you ran so we can reproduce quickly?

jin: Sure:
```
./bench_kv_cache \
  --gpu-mix "us-west1:A100,eu-west1:H100,asia-east:T4" \
  --seq-mix "short:65,med:25,long:10" \
  --kernels "fmha-default,fmha-flash,fmha-ptx-optim" \
  --prefetcher on --eviction-policy lru --run-id kv-prefetch-1768342100
```

ethan: Good. Next steps: (1) try increasing prefetch window in eu-west1 by 2x, (2) run with `eviction=ttl:200` to reduce churn, (3) surface device memcpy metrics in console for those runs.

jin: On it — scheduling follow-up runs. I'll upload the CSV and a small ascii chart to the benchmark dashboard when done. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
